text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav-Romanian trade can reach $450 million next year and double in the near future, says Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic at the end of a three-day visit to Romania.
- Serbia has 16,114 persons living on unemployment welfare, the figure has been on the rise from May to August this year, says the Serbian labour market office.
- "It is realistic to expect the export volume of $1.46 billion in 1995 to be considerably exceeded this year," says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Slobodan Babic.
- Bosnian Serb Parliament Speaker Momcilo Krajisnik said Serbs wish to paticipate in joint bodies of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Dayton agreement to be consistently implemented.
- Workers of the wagon factory Vagonka DD, part of Machine Industry Nis, MIN Nis, continue strike, says member of presidency of the independent trade union Bojko Vucic.
- Solution for Kosovo is for it to gain independence but without war, say three Kosovo Albanian leaders at round table in Belgrade.
- Director General of Bar port Petrasin Kasalica says he expects the port to operate with full capacity when outer wall of sanctions is lifted and large production systems in Serbia restart.
- There is no alternative to market economy which cannot exist without private ownership, said Montenegrian Prime Minsiter Milo Djukanovic in Budva.

- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan MIlutinovic arrives in New York to attend U.N. General Assembly. He will have a series of important meetings and discuss among other issues Yugoslavia's return to the United Nations.
- There is no need for the devaluation of the dinar, says deputy governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia Bozidar Gazivoda.
